title: The Reformation
summary: A monk's challenge to the Church splits Western Christendom and reshapes politics, culture, and belief across Europe.

stories.title: Luther's Revolt
stories.summary: From the 95 Theses to the Peace of Augsburg — the birth of Protestant Europe.

events.title: 95 Theses
events.body: Martin Luther nailed his Ninety-five Theses to the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg, attacking the sale of indulgences. The document spread across Germany within weeks, igniting a debate the Church could not contain.

events.title: Diet of Worms
events.body: Summoned before Emperor Charles V, Luther refused to recant: 'Here I stand, I can do no other.' The Edict of Worms declared him an outlaw, but princes who shared his views offered him protection.

events.title: Peasants' War
events.body: Inspired partly by Reformation rhetoric of spiritual equality, peasants across Swabia and Thuringia rose against feudal obligations. Luther condemned the revolt; princes crushed it at Frankenhausen with tens of thousands dead.

events.title: Augsburg Confession
events.body: Presented to Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg, the Confession defined Lutheran doctrine in twenty-eight articles. It became the foundational statement of faith for Protestant churches across northern Europe.

events.title: Peace of Augsburg
events.body: The Peace of Augsburg ended decades of religious war in the Empire with the formula cuius regio, eius religio — each prince would determine his territory's faith. Protestantism was now a permanent fact of European politics.

stories.title: Counter-Reformation
stories.summary: The Catholic Church responds with reform, renewal, and the Council of Trent.
